items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: She followed-- before that they had a woman working opposite us by the name of Cleo Brown... [Lo Palma] But Gladys LaPalmer was going with the door man who was a great, big black guy. His name was Jumbo.

ctx.x: sneak and smoke and my mother was aware that I was smoking. But after a while she was, but she never said anything to me about it, you know, but I knew that she knew. Well, I never did smoke in front of her.

But when I started working at the three Deuces, then everybody smoked, you know. Nance would come down and work, and we'd smoke and burn our incense on the bandstand. Nobody -- you know, we'd smoke right on the bandstand, it didn't make any difference, you know. But there was a girl [Lo Palma] working there at the time, Gladys LaPalmer.
